title: Purchase Order, GRN and Invoice Three-Way Matching
summary: Read supplier invoices, match every line to POs and GRNs in SAP or Tally, check GST details and tolerances, propose debit notes and send only real exceptions to accounts payable.

seo.title: PO, GRN and Invoice Three-Way Matching with AI | VipraTech
seo.description: AI reads supplier invoices, matches lines to POs and GRNs in SAP or Tally, checks GST and tolerances, and routes only real exceptions to accounts payable.

problem.intro: A plant receives supplier invoices as PDFs, scans and email attachments, often before or after the material is received and inspected. Accounts payable has to tie each invoice line to the PO and to the GRN quantity that quality accepted, then sort out short supply, rejections and price differences before anything is posted.

pain_points.title: Many formats, many lines
pain_points.detail: Each supplier's invoice layout differs, and one invoice can carry dozens of lines with HSN codes, tax splits, freight and packing charges.

pain_points.title: Partial deliveries and split GRNs
pain_points.detail: One invoice may cover several GRNs, or one GRN several invoices, which makes line-level matching slow and error-prone.

pain_points.title: Variances found late
pain_points.detail: Price or quantity differences and QC rejections surface after posting, leading to debit notes, disputes and strained supplier relations.

pain_points.title: GST credit at risk
pain_points.detail: Invoices with a wrong GSTIN or tax rate, a missing IRN, or no entry in GSTR-2B put input tax credit at risk if they are not caught early.

solution.overview: We build a matching pipeline that reads each supplier invoice, extracts header and line items, and matches them to open PO lines and accepted GRN quantities pulled from SAP or Tally. It handles partial deliveries, several GRNs per invoice and unit-of-measure conversions. Rules check price and quantity against your tolerances, compare GST details with the supplier master and e-invoice data, and flag possible duplicates. Clean invoices are prepared as parked documents or draft vouchers for AP to post. Exceptions go to a queue with a reason code, plus a proposed debit note where quantity was short or rejected.
capabilities: Extracts invoice header, line items, HSN codes, tax splits, freight and TDS-relevant fields
Matches many-to-many across invoice lines, PO lines and GRNs, including unit conversions
Applies price and quantity tolerances per supplier or material group
Checks GSTIN, tax rate and place of supply, and reads the e-invoice QR code where present
Detects duplicate invoices by supplier, number, date and amount, including re-sent scans
Proposes debit notes for short supply, QC rejections and price differences with evidence attached

workflow.title: Capture invoices
workflow.detail: Invoices arrive from the AP mailbox, a supplier portal or scans at the inward gate and are grouped by supplier.

workflow.title: Extract and validate
workflow.detail: OCR and an LLM extract header and line data, each field with a confidence score and page reference.

workflow.title: Match to PO and GRN
workflow.detail: Lines are matched to open PO lines and accepted GRN quantities from SAP or Tally.

workflow.title: Apply tolerance and GST checks
workflow.detail: Price, quantity, tax and duplicate rules run, and each failure gets a reason code.

workflow.title: AP review of exceptions
workflow.detail: AP sees the invoice, PO and GRN side by side and resolves the exception or escalates it to purchase.

workflow.title: Prepare for posting
workflow.detail: Matched invoices are created as parked documents or draft vouchers, with debit note proposals where needed.

Open purchase orders and schedule lines from SAP or Tally
GRN and QC acceptance data, including rejected quantities

human_in_the_loop: AP executives resolve every exception and post every invoice; the system prepares documents and never posts or releases payment. Buyers decide price variances, and stores or quality confirm disputed quantities before a debit note is raised.
integrations: SAP S/4HANA or ECC (MM and FI) via BAPI, IDoc or API

Document management system for the invoice archive
guardrails: No auto-posting or payment release; AP approves every document
Uncertain fields and lines flagged, never silently passed
Bank detail changes printed on an invoice are flagged, not accepted
Duplicate checks across suppliers and periods
Every value linked to its source page and every override logged
compliance_notes: Checks support GST input tax credit conditions by comparing invoice data with GSTR-2B and e-invoice details; ITC decisions stay with your tax team.
The audit trail helps evidence internal financial controls over purchase-to-pay for statutory audit.

faqs.q: We use SAP in one plant and Tally in another. Does that matter?
faqs.a: No. The matching logic is the same; only the adapters differ. We read POs and GRNs from each system and write back parked documents or draft vouchers in the format that system expects.

faqs.q: What about invoices with handwritten corrections or poor scans?
faqs.a: They are read like any other invoice, but low-confidence fields are flagged for AP to confirm. The pilot report shows how many invoices needed field confirmation and why.

faqs.q: Can it handle service invoices and job-work charges without a GRN?
faqs.a: Yes, as two-way matches against the PO or a service entry sheet, with their own rules. We usually start with material invoices and add service invoices once the core flow is stable.

faqs.q: Will our supplier and pricing data leave our environment?
faqs.a: It does not have to. The pipeline can run in your cloud tenancy or on-premise, and we use model endpoints that do not retain or train on your data.
